codedokode · Nov 28, 2026

If you want to do large updates to B+tree, you better do it with bulk operations. I made a prototype on paper and in Python (unfinished, fails most of the tests) to do it. You provide a sorted list of deleted keys and sorted list of inserts and walk the B+ tree once, skipping unaffected branches and editing modified nodes. Not that difficult, but there are lot of small nuances. My prototype was using an immutable tree which adds some complexity.
